metadata.name: Whisker Bar Pairing Knowledge Base
metadata.scope: Game-oriented sensory pairing knowledge at drink-style and food-category level.
metadata.important_note: Pairing scores describe flavor compatibility, not medical safety. Intoxication risk depends mainly on total ethanol consumed, pace, body factors and context; mixing different beverage types does not make consumption safe.
metadata.design_note: Use scores as recommendation priors, then modify by customer taste, budget, occasion, region, inventory and explicit restrictions.
sources_basis: Wine Folly pairing principles and cheese/wine examples
Japan Sake and Shochu Makers Association sake pairing guidance

principles.title: Match intensity
principles.rule: Delicate food generally works with lighter drinks; rich or strongly flavored food generally needs a more intense drink.

principles.title: Acidity cuts richness
principles.rule: High-acid wine, cider, beer or cocktails can refresh the palate alongside fatty, creamy or fried food.

principles.title: Drink should not be drier than a sweet dessert
principles.rule: For desserts, choose a drink at least as sweet as the food; otherwise the drink can taste thin or sour.

principles.title: Tannin and fat
principles.rule: Tannic red wines often work well with fatty or protein-rich foods such as steak and aged cheese.

principles.title: Be careful with heat
principles.rule: High alcohol and high tannin can amplify chili heat; aromatic, lower-alcohol or slightly sweet drinks are often easier with spicy food.

principles.title: Salt likes acidity and bubbles
principles.rule: Sparkling wine, crisp beer and acidic drinks are reliable with salty or fried food.

principles.title: Umami needs care
principles.rule: Umami-heavy foods can make tannic wine seem more bitter; sake, sparkling wine, lighter reds and crisp whites are often safer choices.

principles.title: Pair to the sauce
principles.rule: The dominant sauce, spice or preparation can matter more than the base protein.

principles.title: Regional pairing
principles.rule: Traditional drinks and foods from the same region are often useful starting points, but they are not absolute rules.
